walkthroughs.body_html:
The Global Economy — a core area of Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Global Economy brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Global Economy.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Alfred Marshall published 'Principles of Economics' establishing supply-demand analysis in:
A fall in the price of a substitute good causes demand to:
options: Decrease (curve shifts left)
Increase (shifts right)
Stay constant
Become vertical

mcqs.q: What is the technical definition of a recession?
options: A recession is when the stock market crashes.
Two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth — a contraction of the economy.
A recession is when prices fall and people lose jobs.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.

Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.

mcqs.q: Are monopolies always bad for consumers?
options: Monopolies are illegal and always harmful.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
Standard theory says monopolies restrict output and raise prices, but possible benefits include economies of scale, R&D investment and dynamic efficiency.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.
